为哲学家写的简明数学史

A Concise History of Mathematics for Philosophers

John Stillwell, University of San Francisco

摘要

Abstract

本书旨在勾勒数学及其历史的轮廓，并特别着重于那些动摇了数学哲学的事件。它的范围从古希腊发现无理数，一直延伸到十九、二十世纪关于无穷与证明之本性的发现。贯穿全书的主题是：直觉与逻辑、意义与存在，以及离散与连续。这些主题在新的数学发现的影响下不断演变，而它们的演变史在很大程度上就是数学哲学史。

This Element aims to present an outline of mathematics and its history, with particular emphasis on events that shook up its philosophy. It ranges from the discovery of irrational numbers in ancient Greece to the nineteenth- and twentieth-century discoveries on the nature of infinity and proof. Recurring themes are intuition and logic, meaning and existence, and the discrete and the continuous. These themes have evolved under the influence of new mathematical discoveries, and the story of their evolution is, to a large extent, the story of philosophy of mathematics.

关键词：数学，哲学

Keywords: mathematics, philosophy

序言

Preface

自古以来，数学与其哲学之间就一直存在着角力。每当关于数学本性的某种观点似乎已经确立，总会有新的数学发现出现并将其打破。于是，毕达哥拉斯学派“万物皆数”的观点被无理长度的发现所打破，数学哲学不得不扩展，把几何作为一个独立的领域包括进来。但这又引出了一个问题：几何的观点能否与数的观点相调和？如果能，又该如何调和？千百年来，事情就这样一直发展下去。

Since ancient times, there has been a struggle between mathematics and its philosophy. As soon as there seems to be a settled view of the nature of mathematics, some new mathematical discovery comes along to disrupt it. Thus, the Pythagorean view that ‘all is number’ was disrupted by the discovery of irrational lengths, and the philosophy of mathematics had to expand to include a separate field of geometry. But this raised the question, Can the geometric view be reconciled with the numerical view? If so, how? And so it went, for millennia.

在许多情况下，数学的进展迫使人们接受此前被认为不可能或自相矛盾的概念，从而改变了人们对数学的看法。数学就这样扰动了哲学。反过来，哲学则通过指出矛盾、并提出如何澄清概念以消除这些矛盾，使数学保持诚实。有时哲学家与数学家是同一个人——例如笛卡尔、莱布尼茨或波尔查诺——因此人们几乎可以说，数学是哲学中一个特别丰富而稳定的分支。

In many cases, advances in mathematics changed ideas about mathematics, by forcing the acceptance of concepts previously thought impossible or paradoxical. Thus mathematics disrupted philosophy. In the opposite direction, philosophy kept mathematics honest by pointing out contradictions and suggesting how concepts might be clarified in order to resolve them. Sometimes the philosopher and the mathematician were one and the same person – such as Descartes, Leibniz, or Bolzano – so one might almost say that mathematics is an especially rich and stable branch of philosophy.

无论如何，要理解数学哲学的过去与现状，首先必须理解数学及其历史。本书的目的，是对数学及其历史作一简要介绍，并特别着重于那些动摇了数学哲学的事件。如果你愿意，也可以说这是一本关于“写给哲学家的数学”的书。我尽量不采取某种特定的哲学立场，只想说明我相信：数学引导哲学，多于哲学引导数学。作为推论，我相信数学家对哲学作出过重要贡献，即使那并非他们的本意。

At any rate, if one is to understand the past and present state of the philosophy of mathematics, one must first understand mathematics, and its history. The aim of the present Element is to give a brief introduction to mathematics and its history, with particular emphasis on events that shook up its philosophy. If you like, it is a book on ‘mathematics for philosophers’. I try not to take a particular philosophical position, except to say that I believe that mathematics guides philosophy, more so than the other way round. As a corollary, I believe that mathematicians have made important contributions to philosophy, even when it was not their intention.

每一节都以对将要讨论的主题的预览开始，并以一个小节结束，突出该节数学内容所引发的哲学问题。同样的主题在各节中反复出现——直觉与逻辑、意义与存在、离散与连续——但它们在新的数学发现的影响下不断演变。

Each section begins with a preview of topics to be discussed and ends with a section highlighting the philosophical questions raised by the mathematics. The same themes recur from section to section – intuition and logic, meaning and existence, and the discrete and the continuous – but they evolve under the influence of new mathematical discoveries.

专家们也许会惊讶于本书很少甚至没有提及二十世纪显赫一时的各种数学哲学——例如柏拉图主义、逻辑主义、形式主义、唯名论和直觉主义。部分原因是我认为它们都不够充分，但主要原因是我希望在不受标签影响的情况下审视数学哲学。我想尽可能多地呈现在哲学上富有启发的数学，而让读者自己决定应如何用哲学术语对其进行分类和贴标签。我希望本书能为读者提供一面“数学透镜”，借以审视许多哲学问题。

Experts may be surprised that there is little or no mention of philosophies of mathematics that were prominent in the twentieth century – platonism, logicism, formalism, nominalism, and intuitionism, for example. This is partly because I find none of them adequate, but mainly because I hope to look at the philosophy of mathematics without being influenced by labels. I want to present as much philosophically instructive mathematics as possible and leave readers to decide how it should be sorted and labelled in philosophical terms. My hope is that this Element will equip readers with a ‘mathematical lens’ with which to view many philosophical issues.

感谢 Jeremy Avigad、Rossella Lupacchini、Wilfried Sieg 以及一位匿名审稿人提出的有益意见，这些意见带来了许多改进。

I thank Jeremy Avigad, Rossella Lupacchini, Wilfried Sieg, and an anonymous referee for their helpful comments, which have resulted in many improvements.

1 无理数与几何

1 Irrational Numbers and Geometry

预览

PREVIEW

数学哲学中许多问题的源头——证明与真理的本性；数的意义与存在；无穷的作用；以及几何、代数与算术之间的关系——是约公元前300年欧几里得的《几何原本》。《几何原本》最著名的是它的公理化几何，即欧几里得几何，其中包括若干标志性结果的证明，例如勾股定理，以及恰好存在五种正多面体。然而，《几何原本》也包含数论的基本思想，例如素数有无穷多个、求最大公因数的欧几里得算法，以及（与之等价的）唯一素因数分解。

The source of many issues in the philosophy of mathematics – the nature of proof and truth; the meaning and existence of numbers; the role of infinity; and the relation between geometry, algebra, and arithmetic – is Euclid’s Elements from around 300 BCE. The Elements is best known for its axiomatic geometry – Euclidean geometry – which includes proofs of signature results such as the Pythagorean theorem and the existence of exactly five regular polyhedra. However, the Elements also includes fundamental ideas of number theory, such as the existence of infinitely many prime numbers, the Euclidean algorithm for greatest common divisor, and (an equivalent of) unique prime factorization.

在欧几里得的时代，正如今天一样，几何与数论之间存在着一道概念鸿沟——即度量与计数之间、或连续与离散之间的鸿沟。造成这道鸿沟的主要原因是无理量的存在；它们在欧几里得之前由毕达哥拉斯学派发现，到《几何原本》成书时，已成为一套精妙的“比例论”的研究对象。这套理论见于《几何原本》第五卷，在连续与离散之间架起了一座脆弱的桥梁。几个世纪以来，后世数学家的工作逐渐加固了这座桥梁，但这一过程并非没有哲学冲突和数学上的意外。这些问题就是本节和下一节的主题。

In Euclid‘s time, as now, there was a conceptual gulf between geometry and number theory – between measuring and counting, or between the continuous and the discrete. The major reason for this gulf was the existence of irrationals, discovered before Euclid’s time by the Pythagoreans and, by the time of the Elements, the subject of a sophisticated ‘theory of proportions’. This theory, in Book V of the Elements, made a tenuous bridge between the continuous and the discrete. The bridge was gradually strengthened over the centuries by the work of later mathematicians, but not without philosophical conflicts and mathematical surprises. These issues are the subject of this section and the next.

1.1 勾股定理

1.1 The Pythagorean Theorem

勾股定理在人类历史上曾被多次独立发现，出现在若干不同的文化中。因此，如果说有哪一条定理能代表数学——及其普遍性——那就是它了。

The Pythagorean theorem was discovered independently several times in human history, and in several different cultures. So if any theorem typifies mathematics – and its universality – this is it.

图 1 说明了这条定理：（白色）直角三角形斜边上的（灰色）正方形，等于另外两边上的（黑色）正方形之和。图 2 给出了这条定理一个可信的“看图证明”：灰色正方形等于大正方形减去三角形的四个副本，而后者又等于两个黑色正方形之和。该定理的大多数独立发现大概都是如此，事实上，人类视觉系统确实促成了许多数学发现。尽管如此，为此后两千年数学定下方向的，却是通往定理的一条截然不同的公理化道路，我们将在第 1.4 节讨论。

Figure 1 illustrates the theorem: the (grey) square on the hypotenuse of the (white) right-angled triangle is equal to sum of the (black) squares on the other two sides. Figure 2 shows a plausible ‘proof by picture’ of the theorem: the grey square equals the big square minus four copies of the triangle, which in turn equals the sum of the two black squares. Most of the independent discoveries of the theorem were probably like this, and indeed the human visual system has many mathematical discoveries to its credit. Nevertheless, it was the radically different axiomatic path to theorems, discussed in Section 1.4, that set the direction of mathematics for the next 2000 years.

但在公理化道路确立之前，勾股定理已引发了另一项重要的概念发展：长度与数之间的区分。相传毕达哥拉斯学派的哲学是“万物皆数”，其起因是发现整数比支配着音乐的和谐。当人们在几何中发现无理比时——正是由于勾股定理——这一哲学便被推翻了。

But before the axiomatic path was established, the Pythagorean theorem provoked another important conceptual development: a distinction between length and number. Legend has it that the philosophy of the Pythagoreans was ‘all is number’, prompted by the discovery that whole number ratios govern musical harmony. This philosophy was overturned when irrational ratios were found in geometry – because of the Pythagorean theorem.

1.2 无理性

1.2 Irrationality

勾股定理谈论的是平方和——我们将在下文进一步讨论这一运算——但它也间接地告诉我们一些关于长度的事情。特别是，它说明：如果一个三角形两条互相垂直的边长度都是 1，那么它的斜边长度 l 的平方等于 2。用现代记号 l2 表示边长为 l 的正方形，我们有 l2=12+12=2。

The Pythagorean theorem talks about sums of squares – an operation we will say more about below – but indirectly, it also tells us something about lengths. In particular, it says that if a triangle has perpendicular sides of length 1, then its hypotenuse has the length l whose square is 2. Using the modern notation l2 to denote the square of side l, we have l2=12+12=2.

现在（仍使用现代记号），假设 l 是有理数，此时我们可以设 l=m/n，其中 m 和 n 是整数。我们还可以假设 m 与 n 除 1 以外没有公因数，因为任何其他公因数都可以预先从 m 和 n 中约去，而不改变 l。在这些条件下，我们可以通过下面一系列推导得出矛盾（这些推导大概可以追溯到毕达哥拉斯学派，但这类证明已知最早的线索见于亚里士多德的《前分析篇》1.23）：

Now (again using modern notation), suppose that l is rational, in which case we can suppose that l=m/n, where m and n are whole numbers. We can also suppose that m and n have no common divisor except 1, since any other common divisor could be divided out of m and n in advance, without changing l. Under these conditions we can derive a contradiction by the following series of implications (these probably go back to the Pythagoreans, but the first known hint of such a proof is in Aristotle’s Prior Analytics 1.23):

l=m/n⇒2=m2/n2（两边平方）(squaring both sides)⇒2n2=m2（两边同乘以 n²）(multiplying both sides by n²)⇒m2 is even / 是偶数⇒m is even, say, / 是偶数，设 =2p（因为奇数的平方是奇数）(since the square of an odd number is odd)⇒2n2=(2p)2=4p2（把 m = 2p 代入 2n² = m²）(substituting m = 2p in 2n² = m²)⇒n2=2p2⇒n2 is even / 是偶数⇒n is even / 是偶数⇒2 divides both m and n / 同时整除 m 与 n，与没有公因数的假设矛盾。contrary to the assumption of no common divisor.

既然假设 l 是整数之比会导致矛盾，l 就是一个无理长度。希腊人常常这样表述这一点：两直角边相等的直角三角形，其直角边与斜边是不可公度的——它们不是任何共同度量单位的整数倍。

Since it is contradictory to assume that l is a ratio of whole numbers, l is an irrational length. The Greeks often expressed this by saying that the side and hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle with equal sides are incommensurable – not whole number multiples of any common unit of measure.

在毕达哥拉斯学派看来，缺乏共同的长度单位意味着长度不是数，因为在他们那里，“数”就是整数及其比。特别是，长度的和与积未必像数的和与积那样，因此“平方和”这一概念需要澄清。在下一节中，我们将看到欧几里得是如何处理长度的和与积的。

In the view of the Pythagoreans, the lack of a common unit of length meant that lengths are not numbers, because ‘numbers’ to them were whole numbers and their ratios. In particular, sums and products of lengths are not necessarily like sums and products of numbers, so the concept of ‘sum of squares’ needs clarification. In the next section we will see how Euclid handled sums and products of lengths.

1.3 长度与数的运算

1.3 Operations on Lengths and Numbers

毕达哥拉斯之后的希腊数学家既否认无理长度可以是数，又允许它们被平方和相加，因此他们不得不用纯几何的方式来定义和与积。

By denying that irrational lengths could be numbers, yet allowing that they could be squared and added, the Greek mathematicians after Pythagoras had to define sum and product in purely geometric terms.

两个长度之和按图 3 所提示的显而易见的方式定义。长度由两条线段 a 和 b 表示，把这两条线段首尾相接，就得到 a+b。由此容易推出 a+b=b+a 以及 a+(b+c)=(a+b)+c（交换律与结合律）。同样清楚的是，由于长度之和仍是长度，任意多个长度都可以相加。因此，就加法而言，长度的行为与数完全一样。

The sum of two lengths is defined in the obvious way suggested by Figure 3. The lengths are represented by two line segments a and b, and a+b is obtained by joining these segments end to end. It follows easily that a+b=b+a and a+(b+c)=(a+b)+c (commutative and associative laws). It is also clear, since the sum of lengths is a length, that any number of lengths can be added. Thus lengths behave exactly like numbers as far as addition is concerned.

积的行为就没有这么简单了。长度 a 与 b 之积不是一个长度，而是以 a、b 为两条互相垂直的边的矩形。长度 a、b、c 之积则是以 a、b、c 为三条互相垂直的棱的长方体（图 4）。

The behaviour of products is not so simple. The product of lengths a and b is not a length but the rectangle with perpendicular sides a and b. And the product of lengths a, b, and c is the rectangular box with perpendicular sides a, b, and c (Figure 4).

由这些定义显然可得 ab=ba 以及 a(bc)=(ab)c，并且还可以看出 a(b+c)=ab+ac（后者实际上是欧几里得《几何原本》第二卷命题 1 的一个特例）。因此，在和与积有定义的范围内，长度满足与正数相同的运算律。问题在于它们只在有限的范围内有定义，因此长度的代数是残缺的。三个以上长度的积不被允许，因为它们没有几何对应物。同样，只有当各个积具有相同的“维数”，即为相同个数的长度之积时，它们才能相加。

It is clear from these definitions that ab=ba and a(bc)=(ab)c, and it can also be seen that a(b+c)=ab+ac (the latter is actually a special case of Euclid’s Proposition 1 of Book II of the Elements). Thus, to the extent that sum and product are defined, lengths satisfy the same laws as positive numbers. The trouble is that they are defined only to a limited extent, so the algebra of lengths is crippled. Products of more than three lengths are not admitted, because they have no geometric counterpart. Likewise, products can be added only when each is of the same ‘dimension’, that is, a product of the same number of lengths.

最后，还有一个复杂但在几何上很自然的相等概念。例如，它规定：如果矩形 R 可以切割成有限多个三角形，并且这些三角形可以重新拼成 S，那么两个矩形 R 与 S 相等。我们将在下一节进一步讨论欧几里得关于矩形及其他多边形相等的理论。值得注意的是，这一理论对多边形是完全充分的，因为任何两个（现代意义上）面积相等的多边形，在欧几里得的意义上确实相等。然而，正如德恩（1900）所证明的，这一理论对多面体是不充分的。德恩证明了体积相等的立方体与正四面体在欧几里得的意义上并不相等。

Finally, there is a complicated, though geometrically natural, notion of equality. It says, for example, that two rectangles R and S are equal if R can be cut into a finite number of triangles which reassemble to form S. We say more about Euclid’s theory of equality for rectangles, and other polygons, in the next section. Remarkably, this theory is perfectly adequate for polygons, because any two polygons of equal area (in the modern sense) are actually equal in Euclid’s sense. However, the theory is not adequate for polyhedra, as was shown by Dehn (1900). Dehn showed that a cube and regular tetrahedron of equal volume are not equal in Euclid’s sense.

1.4 公理化方法

1.4 Axiomatics

约翰·奥布里在他的《名人小传》中谈到托马斯·霍布斯时，生动地描述了公理化方法的力量：

The power of the axiomatic method is charmingly described by John Aubrey in his Brief Lives, speaking of Thomas Hobbes:

他四十岁时才第一次看几何书；那纯属偶然。在一位绅士的书房里……欧几里得的《几何原本》正摊开着，翻在第一卷第 47 命题。他读了这个命题。“天哪，”他说，“这不可能！”于是他去读它的证明，证明让他回头参考某个命题；他又读了那个命题。那个命题又让他回头参考另一个命题，他也读了……最后，他通过证明确信了那条真理。这使他爱上了几何。
He was 40 yeares old before he looked on geometry; which happened accidently. Being in a gentleman’s library … Euclid’s Elements lay open, and ’twas the 47 Elements, Book I. He read the proposition. ‘By G–’, sayd he, ‘this is impossible!’ So he reads the demonstration of it, which referred him back to such a proposition; which proposition he read. That referred him back to another, which he also read … that at last he was demonstratively convinced of that trueth. This made him in love with geometry.

顺便一提，第一卷第 47 命题就是勾股定理。《几何原本》是流传至今的第一部系统阐述定理与证明的著作，在此后两千年里，它成为西方世界（后来还有伊斯兰世界）表述数学的标准方式。

Proposition 47 of Book I, incidentally, is the Pythagorean theorem. The Elements is the first systematic account of theorems and proofs that has come down to us, and it became the standard way of presenting mathematics in the Western world (and later the Islamic world) for the next 2000 years.

欧几里得从少数几条基本假设（公理）出发，用逻辑从中推出全部定理。他的公理包括关于点、直线、长度和角的简单陈述。还有关于相等、加法和减法的陈述，例如“等于同一事物的事物彼此相等”和“等量加等量，其和相等”。逻辑原理则没有明确陈述。最重要的公理是平行公理，勾股定理和许多其他定理都需要它。按照希思（1956）的译文，欧几里得是这样陈述的：

Euclid begins with a small number of basic assumptions (axioms) and deduces all theorems from them by logic. His axioms include simple statements about points, lines, length, and angle. There are also statements about equality, addition, and subtraction, such as ‘things which are equal to the same thing are equal to each other’ and ‘if equals be added to equals then the wholes are equal’. The principles of logic are not explicitly stated. The most important axiom, needed for the Pythagorean theorem and many others, is the parallel axiom. Euclid states it as follows, in the translation by Heath (1956):

如果一条直线与两条直线相交，使同侧的两个内角之和小于两直角，那么这两条直线无限延长后，必在内角和小于两直角的那一侧相交。
That, if a straight line falling on two straight lines make the interior angles on the same side less than two right angles, the two straight lines, if produced indefinitely, meet on that side on which are the angles less than two right angles.

这段相当冗长的陈述可由图 5 说明。直线 n 与直线 l、m 相交，在右侧形成角 α 和 β，且 α+β<π。结论是 l 与 m 必在右侧某处相交。因此，平行公理实际上给出的是直线不平行的一个条件。

This rather long-winded statement is illustrated in Figure 5. The line n falls on the lines l and m, making angles α and β on the right with α+β<π. The conclusion is that l and m then meet somewhere on the right. Thus the parallel axiom actually gives a condition for lines not to be parallel.

由此可以推出（并不十分显然）：过给定直线 l 外的一个给定点 P，恰好有一条直线与 l 平行，即满足 α+β=π 的直线 m。

It follows (not quite obviously) that there is exactly one parallel to a given line l through a given point P outside l, namely the line m for which α+β=π.

平行公理的复杂性质激起了许多尝试，试图通过证明它可由欧几里得的其他公理推出而将其消除。但所有这类尝试都失败了。这在十九世纪导致了对公理化方法的彻底审视，以及随后对其范围与局限的分析。我们稍后再接着讲这个故事。

The complicated character of the parallel axiom provoked many attempts to eliminate it by showing that it follows from Euclid’s other axioms. But all such attempts failed. This led, in the nineteenth century, to a thorough examination of the axiomatic method and to subsequent analysis of its scope and limits. We pick up this story later.

1.5 哲学问题

1.5 Philosophical Issues

相传毕达哥拉斯学派最早提出了一种数学哲学，实际上是一种非常简单的“万有理论”：万物皆数。据说他们观察到整数在音乐和谐中的作用，并由此一跃得出结论：整个宇宙都由整数及其比所支配。这种哲学的回声至今仍可在“天体的和谐”之类的说法中听到。

According to legend, the Pythagoreans were the first to propose a philosophy of mathematics, in fact a very simple ‘theory of everything’: all is number. It is said that they observed the role of whole numbers in musical harmony and jumped from there to the conclusion that the whole universe is ruled by whole numbers and their ratios. The echoes of this philosophy are still heard in phrases like ‘the harmony of the spheres’.

无论其细节如何，毕达哥拉斯学派的哲学被 2 这类无理量的发现所打破。无理量作为数是不可接受的，但在几何中却是不可避免的，因为没有人能否认：如果正方形存在，那么它的对角线也存在。这导致了《几何原本》中所见的数论与几何的分离，也导致了《几何原本》第五卷中的那套理论。第五卷中的“比例论”在（有理）数与几何量之间建立了一个接触点，尽管并没有完全调和二者。

Whatever its details may have been, the Pythagorean philosophy was disrupted by the discovery of irrational quantities such as 2. Irrationals were unacceptable as numbers, but unavoidable in geometry, since no one could deny that if a square exists, then so does its diagonal. This led to the separation of number theory and geometry seen in Euclid’s Elements but also to the theory found in the Elements Book V. The ‘theory of proportions’ found in Book V establishes a point of contact between (rational) numbers and geometric quantities, though without fully reconciling the two.

此后数学及其哲学的大部分历史，都源于调和数与量、离散与连续、或理性（逻辑）与视觉（直觉）这些概念的努力。正如我们将在后面各节看到的，数学哲学的发展一直伴随着这一努力。

Much of the subsequent history of mathematics, and its philosophy, grows from the struggle to reconcile the concepts of number and quantity, or the discrete and the continuous, or the rational (logical) and the visual (intuitive). The development of mathematical philosophy accompanies this struggle, as we will see in the sections that follow.

在每一节的末尾，我都会以“直觉与逻辑”“意义与存在”“离散与连续”为标题，对哲学的发展作一个可以说是历史性的更新。作为数学家，我更喜欢用这些术语来思考，但我希望哲学家们能把我所说的哲学内容转译成他们自己偏爱的术语。

At the end of each section I will give a historical update, as it were, of philosophical developments, under the headings of logic and intuition, meaning and existence, and discrete and continuous. As a mathematician, I prefer to think in these terms, but I hope that philosophers will be able to translate the philosophical content of my remarks into their own preferred terms.

直觉与逻辑。欧几里得的《几何原本》大概是为了精确地处理几何量，成为已知最早的以公理化方法求真理的范例：定理由公理经逻辑推出。然而，他的公理并不完备，书中频频诉诸直觉，甚至第一个命题中就有一次。因此，《几何原本》无意中说明了在数学推理中避免不自觉的假设是多么困难。

Intuition and logic. Probably in an attempt to work precisely with geometric quantities, Euclid’s Elements is the first known example of the axiomatic approach to truth, whereby theorems are deduced from axioms by logic. However, his axioms are incomplete, and there are frequent appeals to intuition, one even in his first proposition. Thus the Elements unintentionally illustrates how hard it is to avoid unconscious assumptions in mathematical reasoning.

意义与存在。欧几里得还试图定义“点”和“线”之类的原始概念，从而削弱了我们今天所理解的公理化方法。他还基本上把“数”的概念限制在自然数及其比上。2 的无理性被认为使它没有资格成为一个数，但欧几里得并没有规定数应当具有哪些性质。

Meaning and existence. Euclid also undercuts what we now consider to be the axiomatic method by attempting to define primitive concepts such as ‘point’ and ‘line’. He also restricts the concept of ‘number’ essentially to the natural numbers and their ratios. The irrationality of 2 is thought to disqualify it from being a number, but Euclid did not prescribe what the properties of numbers should be.

离散与连续。由于对无理量的敏感，《几何原本》一般把数与量的概念、或离散与连续的概念清楚地分开。但正如我们稍后将看到的，第五卷开启了二者融合的一种可能。

Discrete and continuous. Because of its sensitivity to irrational quantities, the Elements generally makes a clear separation between the concepts of number and quantity, or between the discrete and the continuous. But Book V begins a possible merger between the two, as we will see later.

这说明了数学与哲学有时相反的倾向。数学家一般持有庞加莱在 1908 年所表达的看法：

This illustrates the sometimes opposing tendencies of mathematics and philosophy. Mathematicians generally have the outlook expressed by Poincaré in 1908:

我想我已经在某处说过，数学是给不同的事物以相同名称的艺术。只要这些事物质料不同而形式相似，就足以让它们可以说是用同一个模子浇铸出来。当语言选择得当时，人们会惊讶地发现，对一个已知对象所作的一切证明，都立即适用于许多新的对象：什么都不需要改变，甚至连术语也不用改，因为名称已经变得相同了。（见 Poincaré 1952，第 34 页）
I think I have already said somewhere that mathematics is the art of giving the same name to different things. It is enough that these things, though differing in matter, should be similar in form, to permit of their being, so to speak, run in the same mould. When language has been well chosen, one is astonished to find that all demonstrations made for a known object apply immediately to many new objects: nothing requires to be changed, not even the terms, since the names have become the same. (see Poincaré 1952, 34)

换言之，如果事物具有相同的行为，数学家就认为它们是相同的。然而，哲学家喜欢作出区分：他们寻找事物不应被视为相同的理由。有时某种区分似乎是有道理的，例如希腊人对数与长度等几何量的区分。但数学总是在可能的地方力图抹去区分。实数概念的漫长演变，可以看作一项抹去数与量之间区分的工程，并随之抹去实数理论与几何之间的区分。

In other words, mathematicians consider things to be the same if they have the same behaviour. Philosophers, however, like to make distinctions: they look for reasons why things should not be considered the same. Sometimes a distinction seems to be justified, as was the Greek distinction between numbers and geometric quantities such as length. But mathematics seeks to erase distinctions where possible. The long evolution of the real number concept can be viewed as a project to erase the distinction between number and quantity and, with it, the distinction between real number theory and geometry.

2 希腊数学中的无穷

2 Infinity in Greek Mathematics

预览

PREVIEW

尽管在《几何原本》中数与长度大多被分开处理，但有一个过程欧几里得同时用于二者——欧几里得算法，它对一对量进行“反复以大减小”的操作。当应用于一对正整数（或更一般地，单位长度的一对正整数倍）时，该算法会终止，因为正整数不可能无限递减。但当应用于一对比值为无理数的长度时，该算法不会终止。事实上，欧几里得正是把其算法的不终止用作无理性的判据，从而把无穷带入了对无理性的讨论。

Although number and length are mostly kept separate in the Elements, there is one process that Euclid applied to both – the Euclidean algorithm, which operates on a pair by ‘repeatedly subtracting the smaller from the larger’. When applied to a pair of positive integer numbers (or more generally, to a pair of positive integer multiples of a unit length) the algorithm terminates because positive integers cannot decrease forever. But when applied to a pair of lengths in irrational ratio, the algorithm does not terminate. Indeed, Euclid used non-termination of his algorithm as a criterion for irrationality, thus bringing infinity into the discussion of irrationality.

欧几里得用来证明勾股定理的那套不依赖数的面积理论，对多边形的面积相当顺利。但类似的方法用于体积时，即使对四面体这样简单的多面体也会失效。欧几里得通过把四面体分解为无穷多个棱柱，求出了它的体积，从而把无穷带入了体积理论。

The number-free theory of area, used by Euclid to prove the Pythagorean theorem, works quite smoothly for areas of polygons. But a similar approach to volume fails for even simple polyhedra, such as the tetrahedron. Euclid was able to find the volume of the tetrahedron by decomposing it into infinitely many prisms, thus bringing infinity into the theory of volume.

希腊的面积理论在处理曲边区域时也有困难，因为曲边区域显然不能分解为有限多个多边形。然而，阿基米德通过把抛物线弓形分解为无穷多个三角形，求出了它的面积。尽管如此，希腊人仍力图“回避无穷”，用任意的有限和来代替无穷和。

The Greek theory of area also had difficulty with curved regions, which obviously cannot be decomposed into finitely many polygons. However, Archimedes was able to find the area of a parabolic segment by decomposing it into infinitely many triangles. Nevertheless, the Greeks sought to ‘avoid infinity’ by considering arbitrary finite sums instead of infinite sums.

2.1 无理性与不终止

2.1 Irrationality and Non-termination

欧几里得算法在《几何原本》第七卷中被引入，作为求两个正整数最大公因数的方法。如欧几里得所说，人们“不断地以大减小”；更确切地说，若 a>b，就把数对 a,b 替换为 a−b,b。由于正整数不可能无限递减，该算法总会终止。例如，对数对 13, 8，可得

The Euclidean algorithm is introduced in Book VII of the Elements, as a method for finding the greatest common divisor of two positive integers. As Euclid says, one ‘continually subtracts the less from the greater’; more precisely, if a>b, one replaces the pair a,b by a−b,b. Since positive integers cannot decrease forever, the algorithm always terminates. For example, with the pair 13, 8, one gets

13,8→5,8→5,3→2,3→2,1→1,1.

当得到一对相同的数时，这个数就是 gcd⁡(a,b)，因为该数对的所有公因数在减法中都得以保持。因此，我们的例子表明 gcd⁡(13,8)=1。

When a pair of identical numbers is obtained, that number is gcd⁡(a,b), because all common divisors of the pair are preserved by subtraction. Thus our example shows that gcd⁡(13,8)=1.

在《几何原本》第十卷中，欧几里得把这一算法推广到长度 a 和 b，此时它可能不终止。例如，（用现代记号）若长度为 a=2 和 b=1，则前两步为

In Book X of the Elements Euclid generalizes the algorithm to lengths a and b, in which case it may not terminate. For example, if (using modern notation) the lengths are a=2 and b=1, then the first two steps are

2,1→1,2−1→2−2,2−1.

此时可以注意到，2−2 与 2−1 之比等于 2 与 1 之比。不清楚希腊人是否注意到了这一点（尽管他们大概知道某种类似的事实），但由初等代数这是显然的，因为

At this point it may be noticed that 2−2 and 2−1 are in the same ratio as 2 and 1. It is not clear whether the Greeks noticed this (though they were probably aware of something similar), but it is clear by basic algebra because

2−2=2(2−1).

既然 2−2 与 2−1 之比等于 2 与 1 之比，对它们应用欧几里得算法，两步之后又会得到另一对同样比值的数——如此下去，永无止境。

Since 2−2 and 2−1 are in the same ratio as 2 and 1, applying the Euclidean algorithm to them will produce, in two steps, yet another pair in that ratio – and so on, forever.

无论欧几里得是否知道这个特定的例子，他都认识到：对比值为无理数的一对长度，该算法不会终止（第十卷，命题 2）。因此，欧几里得算法通过区分终止与不终止——也就是区分有限与无穷——优雅地把有理与无理区分开来。

Whether or not Euclid knew this particular example, he realized that the algorithm does not terminate on a pair of lengths in irrational ratio (Book X, Proposition 2). Thus the Euclidean algorithm elegantly separates rational from irrational, by separating termination from non-termination; that is, finite from infinite.

2.2 面积与体积

2.2 Areas and Volumes

在《几何原本》第一卷中，欧几里得通过加上或减去相等的三角形来证明各种区域相等。例如，图 6 表明平行四边形等于同底等高的矩形。图 7 则表明三角形等于同底等高的矩形的一半。

In Book I of the Elements Euclid shows equality of various regions by adding or subtracting equal triangles. For example, Figure 6 shows that a parallelogram equals a rectangle of the same base and height. And Figure 7 shows that a triangle equals half a rectangle with the same base and height.

还有一些分解表明：任何矩形都等于一个具有给定底边的矩形。利用这一事实，通过把多边形切割成有限多个三角形，就可以找到一个与任意多边形相等的矩形。现在，如果（像三角形的情形那样）一个区域 R 等于某个可取作单位的标准区域的有理倍数 r，那么按照欧几里得的思路，可以让数 r 来“度量”区域 R，正如我们度量 R 的面积一样。在这些条件下，从现在起我们将谈论数值化的“面积”与“体积”。

There are also decompositions showing that any rectangle equals a rectangle with a given base. Using this fact, it is possible to find a rectangle equal to any polygon, by cutting the polygon into finitely many triangles. Now if (as in the case of the triangle) one region R equals a rational multiple r of some standard region we can take as a unit, then it is compatible with Euclid to let the number r ‘measure’ the region R in the same way that we measure the area of R. Under these conditions we will speak of numerical ‘areas’ and ‘volumes’ from now on.

而曲边区域显然不能切割成有限多个三角形。我们所能期望的最好结果，是把它分解为无穷多个三角形，而如果运气好的话，这种分解或许是可以理解的。阿基米德用这种方法取得了辉煌的成功，求出了抛物线弓形的面积。

Now a curved region obviously cannot be cut into finitely many triangles. The best we can hope for is a decomposition into infinitely many triangles which, if we are lucky, might be comprehensible. Archimedes had a brilliant success by this method, finding the area of a parabolic segment.

抛物线弓形按图 8 所示的方式用三角形填满：先是黑色三角形，然后是它下方的两个深灰色三角形，再是它们下方的四个浅灰色三角形，依此类推。

The parabolic segment is filled with triangles in the manner shown in Figure 8: first the black triangle, then two dark grey triangles below it, then four lighter grey triangles below them, and so on.

每个三角形的宽度是其上方三角形的一半，计算表明，每一组（一个、两个、四个……三角形）的总面积是其上一组面积的四分之一。因此，如果黑色三角形的面积为 1，那么这些三角形的总面积就是无穷和

Each triangle is half the width of the triangle above it, and a calculation shows that each group (of one, two, four, … triangles) has total area one-fourth the area of the group above it. Thus, if the black triangle has area 1, then the total area of the triangles is the infinite sum

1+14+(14)2+(14)3+(14)4+⋯.

如果我们令

If we set

S=1+14+(14)2+(14)3+(14)4+⋯,

那么显然有

then clearly

4S=4+1+14+(14)2+(14)3+(14)4+⋯,

因此 4S−S=4，从而 S=4/3。（这种对无穷和的冒险计算提供了一种猜出答案的快捷方法。我们将在下一节看到阿基米德是如何更审慎地处理它的。）

so 4S−S=4 and therefore S=4/3. (This risky calculation with infinite sums gives a quick way to guess the answer. We will see how Archimedes did it more carefully in the next section.)

四面体则用棱柱来填充，如图 9 所示。取出两个棱柱（一个浅灰色，另一个深灰色）之后，剩下两个较小的四面体，我们再从中取出棱柱，并继续下去。

The tetrahedron is filled with prisms, as indicated in Figure 9. After two prisms are removed (one light grey, the other darker grey), two smaller tetrahedra remain, from which we again remove prisms, and continue.

欧几里得用这种方法求得四面体的体积是一个类似的无穷和，

In this way Euclid found that the volume of the tetrahedron is a similar infinite sum,

14+(14)2+(14)3+(14)4+⋯,

它等于 1/3。

which equals 1/3.

2.3 穷竭法

2.3 The Method of Exhaustion

前两节展示了希腊数学中无穷过程的例子。上一节中的例子之所以引人注目，是因为它们求出了一个看来无法通过有限过程得到的有理面积或体积。尽管如此，希腊人对无穷心存疑虑，并尽可能地回避它。在许多情况下，他们能够借助所谓的穷竭法做到这一点。

The last two sections have shown examples of infinite processes in Greek mathematics. Those in the previous section are notable for finding a rational area or volume apparently not obtainable by finite processes. Nevertheless, the Greeks were suspicious of infinity and they tried to avoid it as far as possible. In many cases they were able to do so by what is called the method of exhaustion.

这种方法之所以得名，是因为人们通过穷尽所有其他可能性（小于 x 或大于 x）来确认由无穷过程得到的结果 x。通常，其他可能性是通过假设该过程运行任意但有限的步数来穷尽的。我们可以用阿基米德求抛物线弓形面积的例子来说明穷竭法，把其中的无穷过程替换为任意的有限过程。这个例子所涉及的无穷过程如下：

The method is so called because one confirms a result x, obtained by an infinite process, by exhausting all other possibilities (less than x or greater than x). Typically, the other possibilities are exhausted by supposing the process to run for an arbitrary, but finite, number of steps. We can illustrate the method of exhaustion in the case of Archimedes’ evaluation of the area of a parabolic segment, replacing the infinite processes by arbitrary finite ones. The infinite processes involved in this example are as follows:

  1. 用无穷多个三角形填满抛物线弓形。我们可以通过证明抛物线内的任一给定点都落在某个三角形之内，来论证这些三角形确实填满了（或“穷竭”了）弓形。这是一个纯粹有限的论证，尽管有些繁琐。
  2. 证明无穷级数 1+14+(14)2+(14)3+(14)4+⋯ 的和为 4/3。
  1. Filling the parabolic segment with infinitely many triangles. We can argue that the triangles do fill the segment (or ‘exhaust’ it) by showing that any given point inside the parabola falls inside some triangle. This is a purely finite, if tedious, argument.
  2. Showing that the infinite series 1+14+(14)2+(14)3+(14)4+⋯ has sum 4/3.

这可以通过求出如下有限和来完成：

This can be done by finding the finite sum

Sn=1+14+(14)2+⋯+(14)n=43−13(14)n.

我们看到，取任意大的 n 值，Sn 就“穷竭”了所有小于 4/3 的数，因为此时 (14)n 变得任意小。而 Sn 显然不能大于 4/3，因此剩下的值 4/3 必然就是该无穷级数的和。

We see that Sn ‘exhausts’ all numbers <4/3 by taking arbitrarily large values of n, because (14)n then becomes arbitrarily small. And obviously Sn cannot be >4/3, so the value that remains, 4/3, is necessarily the sum of the infinite series.

因此，抛物线弓形的面积（类似地，四面体的体积）可以用任意的有限和而非无穷和求出。这是希腊人回避实际使用无穷的典型方式。我们将在下一节看到类似的“对无穷的回避”。

Thus the area of the parabolic segment (and similarly the volume of the tetrahedron) can be found by using arbitrary finite sums instead of infinite sums. This is typical of the way the Greeks avoided actual use of infinity. We will see a similar ‘avoidance of infinity’ in the next section.

2.4 比例论

2.4 The Theory of Proportions

《几何原本》读者的一个常见绊脚石是第五卷，即所谓的比例论。这一理论被认为出自欧多克索斯，涉及长度概念及其与数的概念的关系。它的主要困难，基本上就是我们今天试图理解实数轴时所遇到的困难。还有一个较小的困难，源于希腊人习惯于处理（整数或长度的）比，这使他们无法使用有理数和单位长度。但为了集中讨论主要困难——当然就是无理量的存在——我将略过这一点，而直接承认有理数和单位长度。

A common stumbling block for readers of the Elements was Book V, on the so-called theory of proportions. This theory, thought to be due to Eudoxus, is about the concept of length and its relation to the concept of number. Its main difficulty is basically the difficulty we meet today in trying to understand the real number line. There is a lesser difficulty due to the Greek habit of working with ratios (of integers or lengths), which stopped them from working with rational numbers and a unit length. But I will gloss over this in order to concentrate on the main difficulty – which is of course the existence of irrationals – by admitting rational numbers and a unit of length.

一旦承认有理数，就会清楚地看出它们是比例论的关键要素。给定单位长度 1，对任意正整数 m,n，我们也就有了有理长度 l=m/n。它是这样一个长度：l 的 n 个副本等于 1 的 m 个副本。对任意长度 a 和 b，这些有理长度决定了 a<b、a=b 还是 a>b。即：

When rational numbers are admitted it becomes clear that they are the key ingredient in the theory of proportions. Given a unit length 1, we also have a rational length l=m/n for any positive integers m,n. It is the length such that n copies of l equal m copies of 1. These rational lengths determine, for any lengths a and b, whether a<b, a=b, or a>b. Namely

a<b⇔存在有理数 m/n 使得 / there is a rational m/n with a<m/n<ba>b⇔存在有理数 m/n 使得 / there is a rational m/n with a>m/n>ba=b⇔既非 a<b 亦非 a>b / neither a<b nor a>b.

因此，若 a<b 或 a>b，就有一对 m,n 可以“见证”这一事实：或者因为 a<m/n<b，或者因为 a>m/n>b。但若 a=b，就没有单独一个有理数 m/n 能见证这一事实（除非 a 和 b 是有理的）：只有当所有小于 a 的有理数都小于 b，并且反之亦然时，a 才等于 b。因此，相等比不等更难以把握，无理长度也比有理长度更难以把握。

Thus if a<b or a>b, there is a pair m,n that ‘witnesses’ the fact: either because a<m/n<b or a>m/n>b. But if a=b, there is no single rational number m/n that witnesses this fact (unless a and b are rational): a equals b only if all rational numbers less than a are less than b, and conversely. Thus equality is more elusive than inequality, and irrational lengths are more elusive than rational lengths.

由于对无穷的疑虑，希腊人没有迈出这样一步：宣称一个无理长度由它两侧的有理长度所确定，因为这种确定涉及无穷多个有理长度。在第 6 节中，我们将看到十九世纪迈出这一步时发生了什么。

Because of their suspicion of infinity, the Greeks did not take the step of saying that an irrational length is determined by the rational lengths on either side of it, since this determination involves infinitely many rational lengths. In Section 6 we will see what happened when this step was taken, in the nineteenth century.

即使是不等的检验，也引出了一个有趣的哲学要点。假设 0<b，从而对某些正整数 m 和 n 有 0<m/n<b。两边同乘以 n，得 0<m<nb。因此，比例论假定了后来所谓的阿基米德公理，即无穷小不存在：若 b>0，则某个整数倍 nb>1。这在十七世纪成了一个热门问题，当时数学家们发现假定无穷小存在很方便；也就是说，他们设想存在 b>0，使得没有任何整数倍 nb>1（见第 4.3 节）。

Even the test for inequality raises an interesting philosophical point. Suppose that 0<b and hence that 0<m/n<b for some positive integers m and n. It follows, multiplying by n, that 0<m<nb. Thus the theory of proportions assumes what would later be called the Archimedean axiom or non-existence of infinitesimals: if b>0 then some integer multiple nb>1. This became a hot issue in the seventeenth century, when mathematicians found it convenient to assume the existence of infinitesimals; that is, they supposed there were b>0 such that no integer multiple nb>1 (see Section 4.3).

2.5 阿基米德与实无穷

2.5 Archimedes and Actual Infinity

与穷竭法一样，比例论也通过转而处理“任意有限”的东西来回避无穷。特别地，它用任意的有限整数 m,n 来见证 a<b，因为 a<m/n<b。事实上，当要证明 a=b 时，用的就是穷竭法；即证明对任何可能的数对 m,n，a<m/n<b 和 a>m/n>b 都不成立。

Like the method of exhaustion, the theory of proportions avoids infinity by dealing instead with the ‘arbitrary finite’. In particular, it employs the arbitrary finite integers m,n to witness that a<b because a<m/n<b. Indeed, when a=b is proved it is done by exhaustion; namely, by showing that a<m/n<b and a>m/n>b fail for any possible pair m,n.

能以这种方式被有限部分“穷竭”的无穷，希腊人称之为“潜无穷”，而在数学论证中只允许使用潜无穷。穷竭法的目的就是回避实无穷；也就是说，回避把一个无穷的集合或过程看作一个完成了的整体。

An infinity that can be ‘exhausted’ in this way by finite parts was called a ‘potential infinity’ by the Greeks, and only potential infinities were allowed in mathematical argument. The aim of the method of exhaustion was to avoid actual infinity; that is, viewing an infinite collection or process as a completed whole.

在欧几里得之后的两千多年里，数学家的官方做法是只接受潜无穷，并借助穷竭法来回避实无穷。这是理论上的做法，但在实践中，实无穷常被用作获得结果的捷径，（人们希望）这些结果以后可以用穷竭法严格证明。

For over 2000 years after Euclid the official practice of mathematicians was to accept only potential infinities, and to avoid actual infinities by appealing to the method of exhaustion. This was the theory, but in practice actual infinities were often used as a shortcut to results that (hopefully) could later be proved rigorously by the method of exhaustion.

就我们所知，最早使用实无穷的是阿基米德，见于他名为《方法》的著作。这部著作失传湮没了好几个世纪，直到 1906 年才被重新发现，因此它对数学及其哲学的发展没有产生影响。然而，它确实表明，希腊人关于无穷的思考比人们从欧几里得那里得到的印象要丰富。阿基米德远远超越了认为一系列离散步骤可以完成的想法；他甚至愿意把直线上点的连续统看作一个完成了的集合（尽管他大概没有意识到连续统是一种新的无穷）。

As far as we know, the first to use actual infinities was Archimedes, in a work called The Method. This work was lost and unknown for centuries before being rediscovered in 1906, so it did not influence the development of mathematics or its philosophy. However, it does show that there was more to Greek thinking about infinity than one would gather from Euclid. Archimedes went far beyond thinking that a sequence of discrete steps could be completed; he was even willing to view the continuum of points on the line as a completed collection (though probably without realizing that the continuum is a new kind of infinity).

2.6 哲学问题

2.6 Philosophical Issues

欧几里得洞悉了有理与无理之区分的核心：那就是有限与无穷之间的差别。因此，接受无理量的几何，也必须以某种形式接受无穷。于是，几何的逻辑必须找到一种对无穷进行推理的方式。

Euclid penetrated to the heart of the distinction between rational and irrational: it is the difference between finite and infinite. Thus geometry, which accepts irrational quantities, must also accept infinity in some form. So the logic of geometry had to find a way of reasoning about infinity.

直觉与逻辑。希腊人尽可能地避免对无穷进行推理。他们对无穷的恐惧从何而来并不完全清楚，不过芝诺悖论表明这种恐惧在欧几里得之前就已存在，而亚里士多德曾试图揭穿它。穷竭法是数学对这些哲学争论的回应：通过对无穷过程的有限（但任意）阶段进行推理来避免对无穷本身进行推理，并论证这些阶段“穷尽了所有可能性”，只剩下一种——因此这种可能性可以被视为该无穷过程的结果。

Intuition and logic. The Greeks tried as far as possible to avoid reasoning about infinity. The origin of their fear of infinity is not completely clear, though Zeno’s paradoxes show that the fear was present before Euclid’s time, and that Aristotle tried to debunk it. The method of exhaustion was the mathematical response to these philosophical debates: avoid reasoning about infinity by reasoning about finite (but arbitrary) stages of an infinite process, and argue that they ‘exhaust all possibilities’ except one – which possibility can therefore be deemed the result of the infinite process.

意义与存在。因此，穷竭法间接地赋予了无穷过程的结果以意义，而无须承诺实无穷的存在。

Meaning and existence. Thus the method of exhaustion indirectly gives meaning to the result of an infinite process, without commitment to the existence of actual infinity.

连续与离散。具有无穷多个离散步骤的过程可以作为“潜无穷”被接受。但由于拒斥实无穷，希腊人一般远离“连续的无穷”这一观念。阿基米德也许是个例外，因为他似乎愿意把直线上点的连续统看作一个完成了的整体。

Continuous and discrete. Processes with an infinite number of discrete steps could be accepted as ‘potential infinity’. But, in rejecting actual infinity, the Greeks generally stayed well away from the idea of a ‘continuous infinity’. Perhaps Archimedes was an exception, because he seemed willing to accept the continuum of points on the line as a completed whole.

如第 1.5 节所述，哲学的倾向是作出区分，而数学的倾向是在可能之处抹去区分。然而，数学有时会发现哲学（以及以往的数学）未曾预见的区分。无穷就是一个恰当的例子。几千年来，数学接受潜无穷与实无穷的区分，并追随哲学，认为实无穷不可接受。但自十九世纪末以来，实无穷不仅（对大多数数学家而言）变得可以接受，而且还出现了意想不到的、复杂的区分。这引发了关于可接受与不可接受的无穷之间界线应划在何处的新争论。我们将在第 7 节看到这是如何发生的。

As mentioned in Section 1.5, the tendency of philosophy is to make distinctions, while that of mathematics is to erase them where possible. However, mathematics sometimes discovers distinctions that philosophy (and previous mathematics) had not foreseen. Infinity is a case in point. For millennia, mathematics accepted the distinction between potential and actual infinity and, following philosophy, considered actual infinity unacceptable. But since the late nineteenth century, actual infinity has not only become acceptable (to most mathematicians) but also subject to unforeseen and complicated distinctions. This has led to new controversies about where to draw the line between acceptable and unacceptable infinity. We will see how this happened in Section 7.

3 虚数

3 Imaginary Numbers

预览

PREVIEW

几个世纪以来，把 2 这样的量当作数的阻力逐渐消退，这或许是因为代数在印度和伊斯兰世界的兴起。在印度，婆罗摩笈多约于公元 600 年给出了二次方程 ax2+bx+c=0 的本质上现代的解

Resistance to treating quantities such as 2 as numbers gradually eroded over the centuries, possibly because of the rise of algebra in India and the Islamic world. In India, Brahmagupta around 600 CE gave essentially the modern solution

x=−b±b2−4ac2a

人们逐渐接受：正数的平方根本身也是一个数。与此同时，人们不愿使用负数（尽管婆罗摩笈多接受负数），而负数的平方根似乎毫无意义。因此，当 b2−4ac<0 时，说 ax2+bx+c=0 无解似乎是很自然的。

of the quadratic equation ax2+bx+c=0, and it became accepted that the square root of a positive number was itself a number. At the same time, there was reluctance to use negative numbers (though Brahmagupta accepted them), and the square root of a negative number seemed nonsensical. Thus when b2−4ac<0 it seemed natural to say that ax2+bx+c=0 had no solution.

十六世纪，意大利数学家发现了三次方程 x3=px+q 的解，其形式为

Things changed in the sixteenth century when Italian mathematicians discovered the solution of the cubic equation x3=px+q in the form

x=q2+(q2)2−(p3)33+q2−(q2)2−(p3)33.

情况由此改变。这个公式不仅要求接受平方根和立方根，还要求接受负数的平方根——因为有些方程明明有一个显而易见的实数解，却有 (q2)2−(p3)3<0。在很长一段时间里，−1 这样的数被称为“不可能的”，至今仍被称为“虚的”。然而它们在数学中被接受了，至少被用来证明关于实数的结果，因为它们有用，而且（通常）不会导致矛盾。最终，实数与虚数构成的体系在代数上和几何上都被视为自然的。

This formula called not only for acceptance of square roots and cube roots, but also for square roots of negative numbers – because there are equations for which there is an obvious real solution yet (q2)2−(p3)3<0. For a long time, numbers such as −1 were called impossible, and they are still called ‘imaginary’. Yet they were accepted in mathematics, at least to prove results about real numbers, because they were useful and they did not (usually) lead to contradiction. Eventually, the system of real and imaginary numbers came to be viewed as natural, both algebraically and geometrically.

3.1 二次方程与三次方程

3.1 Quadratic and Cubic Equations

正如我们在第 1 节所见，在希腊数学中，代数受到乘积的几何解释的束缚。在几何解释下，三项以上的乘积没有意义，不同维数的乘积不能相加。这些限制并不适用于数的乘积，因此在数的代数与长度的代数之间的较量中，数的代数显然胜出。代数的发展过程大致就是如此；代数最初是一套用于解决关于数的问题（尤其是方程）的符号体系。

As we have seen in Section 1, algebra was hamstrung in Greek mathematics by the geometric interpretation of product. Under the geometric interpretation, products of more than three terms have no meaning, and products of different dimensions cannot be added. These restrictions do not apply to the product of numbers, so in a contest between algebra for numbers and algebra for lengths, algebra for numbers clearly wins. This is roughly what happened in the development of algebra, which was initially a symbolism for solving problems (especially equations) about numbers.

直到约 1600 年，代数一直是一门求解数的方程的学科，但它要退回到几何中去为自己的步骤提供辩护——因为欧几里得的《几何原本》仍是数学证明的典范。

Until about 1600, algebra was a discipline that solved equations in numbers but it fell back on geometry to justify its moves – because Euclid’s Elements was still the model for mathematical proof.

从几何向数的代数的转变始于丢番图，约在公元 200 年，即古典希腊数学的最后阶段。丢番图使用的符号体系允许四个或更多元素的乘积。但由于他感兴趣的是寻找方程的有理解，他只使用有理运算 +,−,×,÷，而不使用平方根运算  。  运算出现在二次方程 ax2+bx+c=0 的通解

The shift from geometry to an algebra of numbers began with Diophantus, around 200 CE, in the last phase of classical Greek mathematics. Diophantus used a symbolism that allowed products of four or more elements. But because he was interested in finding rational solutions of equations he used only the rational operations +,−,×,÷, not the square root operation  . The   operation occurs in the general solution

x=−b±b2−4ac2a(*)

之中。这个解本质上由婆罗摩笈多于约公元 600 年在印度给出，不过用的是文字而非符号。对方程的研究从印度传播到伊斯兰世界，约公元 800 年，花拉子米在那里给它起名为“代数”。由此它又传到意大利，下一个重大进展就发生在那里：三次方程的求解。

of the quadratic equation ax2+bx+c=0. Essentially, this solution was given by Brahmagupta in India around 600 CE, though in words rather than symbols. The study of equations spread from India to the Islamic world, where it was given the name ‘algebra’ by al-Khwarizmi around 800 CE. From there it passed to Italy, where the next major advance occurred: the solution of cubic equations.

x3=px+q 的解约于 1500 年由希皮奥内·德尔·费罗发现，但被当作当时流行的数学竞赛中的“秘密武器”而秘而不宣。塔尔塔利亚在 1530 年代重新发现了它，它首次发表于卡尔达诺的《大术》（1545）。这个所谓的卡尔达诺求解公式是

The solution of x3=px+q was discovered by Scipione del Ferro around 1500 but was kept as a ‘secret weapon’ for the mathematical contests that were then popular. It was rediscovered by Tartaglia in the 1530s and first published in the Ars Magna of Cardano (1545). The so-called Cardano formula for the solution is

x=q2+(q2)2−(p3)33+q2−(q2)2−(p3)33(**)

这时的数学家已经愿意接受正数的平方根和立方根，但对负数的平方根却裹足不前。当然，当 b2<4ac 时，负数的平方根已经出现在二次公式 (*) 中。但在这种情况下，人们可以随意地说方程 ax2+bx+c=0 无解。三次方程的解 (**) 则不然。

Mathematicians by this time were willing to accept square and cube roots of positive numbers, but they balked at square roots of negative numbers. Of course square roots of negative numbers already occur in the quadratic formula (*) when b2<4ac. But in this case one is free to say that the equation ax2+bx+c=0 has no solution. It was otherwise with the solution (**) of the cubic equation.

3.2 邦贝利的虚数代数

3.2 Bombelli’s Algebra of Imaginary Numbers

即使卡尔达诺公式中含有负数 (q2)2−(p3)3 的平方根，方程 x3=px+q 也可能有一个显而易见的解。例如 x3=15x+4 就是如此，它有显而易见的解 x=4。对这个方程，卡尔达诺公式给出（经过一些化简后）

The equation x3=px+q can have an obvious solution, even though the Cardano formula contains the square root of a negative number (q2)2−(p3)3. This is the case, for example, for x3=15x+4, which has the obvious solution x=4. For this equation the Cardano formula gives (after some simplification)

x=2+11−13+2−11−13.

为了让这个表达式与 x=4 这个值相符，邦贝利（1572）假定 −1 服从与普通数相同的代数规则。他对自己的计算秘而不宣，但它很容易重构。用现代记号 i 表示 −1，于是 i2=−1，可以验证

To reconcile this expression with the value x=4, Bombelli (1572) assumed that −1 obeys the same algebraic rules as ordinary numbers. He kept his calculation a secret, but it is easy to reconstruct. Using the modern notation i for −1, so i2=−1, one can check that

(2+i)3=2+11iand / 以及(2−i)3=2−11i;

因此

and therefore

2+11−13+2−11−13=2+11i3+2−11i3=(2+i)33+(2−i)33=(2+i)+(2−i)=4.

正如许多人后来所说的那样，代数似乎比我们更聪明！

As many people have since remarked, it seems as though algebra is smarter than we are!

无论如何，邦贝利的例子以及其他类似的例子，最终使数学家们相信，使用“虚”数或“不可能的”数是安全的。无论 −1 意味着什么（如果它有意义的话），它的行为似乎都像一个普通的数，并且能给出关于普通数的正确结果。

At any rate, Bombelli’s example, and others like it, eventually convinced mathematicians that it was safe to use ‘imaginary’ or ‘impossible’ numbers. Whatever −1 means, if anything, it seems to behave like an ordinary number and to give correct results about ordinary numbers.

3.3 虚数的便利

3.3 The Convenience of Imaginary Numbers

在十八和十九世纪，数学家们发现，在许多情形下，借助虚数可以更容易地陈述或解释普通数的已知性质。下面是一些例子。

In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries mathematicians discovered many situations in which known properties of ordinary numbers are more easily stated, or explained, with the help of imaginary numbers. Here are some examples.

  1. 三角公式 cos⁡(θ+φ)=cos⁡θcos⁡φ−sin⁡θsin⁡φsin⁡(θ+φ)=sin⁡θcos⁡φ+cos⁡θsin⁡φ 可以更简洁（也更好记）地用一个公式来表达：cos⁡(θ+φ)+isin⁡(θ+φ)=(cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ)(cos⁡φ+isin⁡φ).
  2. 如果我们假定 eix=cos⁡x+isin⁡x（这样做的理由见第 4.5 节），那么后一个公式还可以更简洁地表达为 ei(θ+φ)=eiθeiφ。这为正弦和余弦函数赋予了新的意义——它们是虚指数函数的组成部分。
  3. 如果 a,b,c,d 是正整数，那么 a2+b2 与 c2+d2 之积本身也是两个整数平方之和。为了找出后者的两个平方，我们利用 i2=−1 构造虚的因式分解（见下式），其中用到恒等式 x2−y2=(x+y)(x−y)。把两个因式分解结合起来，并再次利用该恒等式，就得到下面的结果。
  1. The trigonometric formulas cos⁡(θ+φ)=cos⁡θcos⁡φ−sin⁡θsin⁡φsin⁡(θ+φ)=sin⁡θcos⁡φ+cos⁡θsin⁡φ are more concisely (and memorably) expressed by the single formula cos⁡(θ+φ)+isin⁡(θ+φ)=(cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ)(cos⁡φ+isin⁡φ).
  2. The latter formula can be even more concisely expressed by ei(θ+φ)=eiθeiφ, if we assume eix=cos⁡x+isin⁡x (see Section 4.5 for a reason to do this). This gives new meaning to the sine and cosine functions – as parts of the imaginary exponential function.
  3. If a,b,c,d are positive integers then the product of a2+b2 and c2+d2 is itself the sum of two integer squares. To find the latter squares we use i2=−1 to create the imaginary factorizations below, using the identity x2−y2=(x+y)(x−y). Combining the factorizations, and again using the identity, we get the result below.
a2+b2=a2−(ib)2=(a+ib)(a−ib)c2+d2=c2−(id)2=(c+id)(c−id),
(a2+b2)(c2+d2)=[(a+ib)(c+id)][(a−ib)(c−id)]=[ac−bd+i(ad+bc)][ac−bd−i(ad+bc)]=(ac−bd)2+(ad+bc)2.

这些例子表明，虚数应当被接受，哪怕只是为了方便。然而，我们还可以做得更好。我们可以给虚数一个令人信服的解释，表明它们与普通数同样“实在”（并顺带解释它们在几何和三角学中的作用）。更保守地说，我们可以说明如何把虚数从任何用到它们的论证中消去，代之以普通数。

These examples suggest that imaginary numbers should be accepted, if only for the sake of convenience. However, it is possible to do better than this. We can give a convincing interpretation of imaginary numbers, which shows them to be just as ‘real’ as ordinary numbers (and incidentally explains their role in geometry and trigonometry). More conservatively, one can show how to eliminate imaginary numbers, from any argument that uses them, in favour of ordinary numbers.

3.4 实现虚数

3.4 Realizing the Imaginary

哈密顿（1835）引入了一种从数学中消去虚数的简单方法：把 a+ib 替换为实数 a,b 的有序对 (a,b)，并把数对的和与积定义为

A simple way to eliminate imaginary numbers from mathematics was introduced by Hamilton (1835): replace a+ib by the ordered pair (a,b) of real numbers a,b, and define the sum and product of pairs by

(a1,b1)+(a2,b2)=(a1+a2,b1+b2)(a1,b1)⋅(a2,b2)=(a1a2−b1b2,a1b2+a2b1).

于是，和 (a1+ib1)+(a2+ib2) 所对应的数对，就是 a1+ib1 与 a2+ib2 所对应数对之和；积所对应的数对同样也是这两个数对之积。由此可知，关于 a+ib 形式的数的和与积的任何陈述，都等价于一个关于实数的陈述，例如

Then the pair for the sum (a1+ib1)+(a2+ib2) is the sum of the pairs for a1+ib1 and a2+ib2, and the pair for the product is likewise the product of the pairs. It follows that any statement about sum and product of numbers of the form a+ib is equivalent to one about real numbers, for example

(a1+ib1)(a2+ib2)=c+id⇔a1a2−b1b2=c and / 且 a1b2+a2b1=d.

因此，任何涉及 i 的论证都可以替换为只涉及实数的论证。正因如此，我们说复数（a+ib 形式的数即称为复数）理论是实数理论的保守扩张。所谓“保守”，是指任何借助 i 证明的关于实数的结果，不借助 i 也能证明。

Hence any argument involving i can be replaced by one involving real numbers alone. Because of this we say that the theory of complex numbers (as the numbers a+ib are called) is a conservative extension of the theory of real numbers. It is ‘conservative’ in the sense that any result about real numbers proved with use of i can be proved without it.

哈密顿的构造表明，假定虚数存在是无害的，但同时也表明，没有必要假定它们存在。凡是我们借助它们能做的事，不借助它们也能做，只是也许没那么容易。

Hamilton’s construction shows that it is harmless to assume that imaginary numbers exist, but at the same time it shows that there is no need to assume they exist. Anything we can do with them we can do without them, though perhaps not as easily.

对大多数数学家来说，使人不得不相信复数的，是它们给出的比我们所要求的更多。仿佛它们一直就是数学结构的一部分，只是起初我们只注意到了其中细小的一缕——三次方程的求解。事实上，i 不仅给出三次方程的解，而且给出所有多项式方程的解。这就是代数基本定理，我们将在第 5 节进一步讨论。

For most mathematicians, what compels belief in the complex numbers is that they give more than we asked for. It is as though they were always part of the fabric of mathematics, but at first we noticed only one small thread in the solution of cubic equations. In fact, i not only gives solutions to cubic equations but to all polynomial equations. This is the fundamental theorem of algebra that we will say more about in Section 5.

此外，虽然 i 不可能位于实数直线上，但让它位于一条与之垂直的虚数直线上却是完全合理的。我们只需想象一个复数平面，其中 a+ib 由点 (a,b) 表示，它到原点 O 的水平距离为 a，垂直距离为 b。在这种解释下，乘以 a+ib 具有一种几何意义，它是 i2=−1 的一个广泛推广。即：乘以 a+ib 把平面放大 a2+b2 倍（a+ib 到 O 的距离），并绕 O 旋转角 θ=tan−1⁡ba。图 10 展示了 a+ib 的几何背景。

Moreover, while i cannot lie on the line of real numbers, it makes perfect sense for it to lie on a perpendicular line of imaginary numbers. All we have to do is imagine a plane of complex numbers, with a+ib represented by the point (a,b) at horizontal distance a from the origin O, and at vertical distance b. Under this interpretation, multiplication by a+ib has a geometric meaning that is a sweeping generalization of i2=−1. Namely multiplication by a+ib magnifies the plane by a2+b2 (the distance of a+ib from O) and rotates it about O through angle θ=tan−1⁡ba. Figure 10 shows a+ib in its geometric context.

特别地，乘以 i 使平面绕 O 旋转一个直角，乘以 cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ 使平面旋转角 θ。因此，复数的乘法囊括了全部基础几何与三角学。

In particular, multiplication by i rotates the plane about O through a right angle, and multiplication by cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ rotates it through angle θ. Thus multiplication of complex numbers encapsulates all of basic geometry and trigonometry.

而这仅仅是开始。如上一节所述，eiθ=cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ，因此复数把三角学与指数函数统一了起来。简而言之，复数大概是高等数学中最强大的统一与简化力量。这就是数学家相信它们的原因。

And this is just the beginning. As mentioned in the previous section, eiθ=cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ; so the complex numbers unite trigonometry with the exponential function. In short, the complex numbers are probably the most powerful unifying and simplifying force in higher mathematics. That is why mathematicians believe in them.

3.5 哲学问题

3.5 Philosophical Issues

代数在印度和伊斯兰世界的兴起，起初并没有影响数学哲学。事实上，直到十六世纪，欧几里得的权威一直统治着代数。伊斯兰代数学家通过诉诸几何图形来为他们的证明辩护，直到卡尔达诺（1545）仍可见到这样的证明。只是到了约十六世纪末，随着现代代数符号的发展，代数计算才成为数学中的一股新力量。

The emergence of algebra in India and the Islamic world did not at first affect the philosophy of mathematics. In fact, Euclid’s authority ruled algebra until the sixteenth century. The Islamic algebraists justified their proofs by appeal to geometric diagrams, and such proofs occur as late as Cardano (1545). It was only around the end of the sixteenth century, when modern algebraic symbolism developed, that algebraic calculation became a new force in mathematics.

符号代数为微积分等其他符号数学分支铺平了道路，数学哲学最终不得不将它们考虑在内。尽管如此，在很长一段时间里，人们仍希望欧几里得可以继续作为数学的基础。

Symbolic algebra paved the way for other branches of symbolic mathematics, such as calculus, which the philosophy of mathematics eventually had to take into account. Nevertheless, for a long time it was hoped that Euclid could remain as the foundation of mathematics.

直觉与逻辑。意大利代数学家起初（与他们的伊斯兰前辈一样）通过诉诸几何逻辑来为代数规则辩护。但邦贝利用 −1 进行的计算表明，代数有它自己独立的逻辑。

Intuition and logic. The Italian algebraists at first justified the rules of algebra (as did their Islamic predecessors) by appeal to geometric logic. But Bombelli’s calculations with −1 suggested that algebra had an independent logic of its own.

意义与存在。虚数起初只被赋予“符号上的存在”，允许它们用于得出实际结果的计算。在成为一套操作符号的规则体系的过程中，代数开始摆脱它的几何基础。然而令人惊讶的是，虚数却为几何提供了新的洞见。

Meaning and existence. Imaginary numbers at first were accorded merely ‘symbolic existence’, allowing them to be used in calculations that had real results. In becoming a system of rules for manipulating symbols, algebra began to break free from its geometric foundation. Yet, surprisingly, imaginary numbers provide new insights into geometry.

离散与连续。希腊人认为只有有理数才真正是数，这一信念在代数（它敦促人们接受平方根和立方根）和三角学（它敦促人们接受正弦和余弦函数）的影响下逐渐瓦解。然而，当时还没有一个融贯的实数理论——只有一种信念，即实数可以用直线上的点来建模。

Discrete and continuous. The Greek belief that only rational numbers were really numbers gradually eroded under the influence of algebra, which urged acceptance of square and cube roots, and of trigonometry, which urged acceptance of the sine and cosine functions. However, there was not yet a coherent theory of real numbers – only the belief that they could be modelled by the points of a line.

4 微积分与无穷小

4 Calculus and Infinitesimals

预览

PREVIEW

代数的影响在十七世纪不断扩大，先是在费马与笛卡尔的代数几何中，然后是在牛顿与莱布尼茨的无穷小微积分中。在几何中，代数迅速解决了有关直线和圆锥曲线的古代问题，并使人们轻松进入了一大类希腊人几乎未曾触及的曲线。

The influence of algebra grew in the seventeenth century, first in the algebraic geometry of Fermat and Descartes, then in the infinitesimal calculus of Newton and Leibniz. In geometry, algebra made quick work of ancient problems about lines and conic sections and gave easy access to a vast class of curves barely touched by the Greeks.

几何的代数方法之所以成为可能，是由于直线和平面的算术化：把直线上的点等同于实数，把平面上的点等同于实数对。在这种等同之下，许多曲线可以用多项式方程 p(x,y)=0 来描述，从而可以通过代数运算来提取几何性质。

The algebraic approach to geometry was made possible by arithmetization of the line and plane: identifying points of the line with real numbers and points of the plane with pairs of real numbers. Under this identification, many curves could be described by polynomial equations, p(x,y)=0, allowing geometric properties to be extracted by algebraic manipulation.

微积分推广了这一思想，允许对无穷小进行代数运算——无穷小是这样一些量：它们在计算中表现得像非零的数，但在其他方面又可以忽略不计。例如，曲线 p(x,y)=0 的斜率可以计算为无穷小 dx 与 dy 之商 dy/dx，其中 dx 被视为 x 的一个无穷小增量，dy 是 y 的相应增量。

Calculus extended this idea by allowing algebraic operations on infinitesimals – quantities that behaved like non-zero numbers in calculations but were otherwise negligible. For example, the slope of a curve p(x,y)=0 could be calculated as a quotient dy/dx of infinitesimals dx and dy, where dx was taken to be an infinitesimal increase in x and dy the corresponding increase in y.

人们赋予无穷小的那些性质，即使不是真的不一致，也已接近不一致。然而，与虚数一样，无穷小似乎用起来既容易又安全。数学家们相信，如果受到质疑，他们可以用更严格的穷竭法重新得到无穷小微积分的结果。无穷小微积分的魔力在于，它能用例行的计算代替复杂的穷竭论证，于是，便利性再一次压倒了对所用数学对象之存在性的一切怀疑。

The properties ascribed to infinitesimals were close to, if not actually, inconsistent. Yet, like imaginary numbers, infinitesimals seemed easy and safe to use. Mathematicians believed that, if challenged, they could reproduce the results of infinitesimal calculus by the more rigorous method of exhaustion. The magic of infinitesimal calculus was its ability to replace complicated exhaustion arguments by routine calculations, so once again convenience overcame any doubts about the existence of the mathematical objects being used.

4.1 无穷级数

4.1 Infinite Series

我们已经看到，欧几里得和阿基米德利用无穷级数之和来求某些面积和体积。这些级数都是无穷等比级数

We have now seen that Euclid and Archimedes used sums of infinite series to find certain areas and volumes. The series in question were instances of the infinite geometric series

a+ar+ar2+ar3+⋯,

的特例；当 |r|<1 时，它的和为 a1−r。这个值可以用穷竭法严格确认。我们求得有限级数

which has sum a1−r when |r|<1. This value can be rigorously confirmed by the method of exhaustion. We find that the finite series

a+ar+ar2+ar3+⋯+arn=a−arn+11−r,

而这个有限和（当 a>0 且 |r|<1 时）显然小于 a1−r，但又能超过任何小于 a1−r 的数，因为选取足够大的 n，就可以使 rn+1 任意小。因此，这些有限和“穷竭”了所有小于 a1−r 的数，所以无穷和必定等于 a1−r。

and this finite sum (for a>0 and |r|<1) is clearly less than a1−r but able to exceed any number less than a1−r, since rn+1 can be made arbitrarily small by choosing n sufficiently large. Therefore, the finite sums ‘exhaust’ all numbers less than a1−r and so the infinite sum must equal a1−r.

当微积分在 1665 年前后被发明时，等比级数是许多其他无穷级数结果的出发点。然而，在微积分发明之前，十五世纪的印度就已发现了三角学中有关无穷级数的惊人结果。这些发现的主要贡献者是马德哈瓦（约 1340—约 1425），他的方法主要是代数的。出发点同样是等比级数，但也巧妙地用到了新的级数，特别是级数

When calculus was invented, around 1665, the geometric series was the starting point for many other results on infinite series. However, before calculus was invented, remarkable results about infinite series in trigonometry were discovered in fifteenth-century India. The main contributor to these discoveries was Madhava (c. 1340–c. 1425) and his methods were largely algebraic. The starting point was again the geometric series, but new series were also used ingeniously, notably the series

1k+2k+3k+⋯+nkfor / 其中 k=1,2,3,….

后一类级数在证明下式时所起的作用，后来由微积分接替：

The latter series played a role later taken over by calculus in proving that

tan−1⁡x=x−x33+x55−x77+⋯for / 当 −1<x≤1.

马德哈瓦还发现了正弦和余弦函数的级数：

Madhava also discovered the series for the sine and cosine functions:

sin⁡x=x−x33!+x55!−x77!+⋯cos⁡x=1−x22!+x44!−x66!+⋯.

后面这些级数以及与之相关的 ex 的级数，在十七世纪的欧洲被重新发现，并在微积分的发展中发挥了重要作用。这些结果在印度和欧洲的独立发现，或许是自勾股定理以来数学文化普遍性最引人注目的例证。

The latter series, and the related series for ex, were rediscovered in Europe in the seventeenth century, and they played an important role in the development of calculus. The independent discovery of these results in India and Europe was perhaps the most remarkable example of the cultural universality of mathematics since the Pythagorean theorem.

4.2 代数几何

4.2 Algebraic Geometry

对数的无穷过程是微积分的一个前提。另一个前提是代数在几何中的应用，简称代数几何。后者在十六世纪代数符号成熟之后才成为可能，那时用多项式进行计算已和用数进行计算一样容易。到 1630 年代，费马和笛卡尔已能为一个今天通常用微积分解决的问题给出代数解法：求代数曲线的切线。

Infinite processes on numbers were one prerequisite for calculus. Another was the application of algebra to geometry, or algebraic geometry for short. The latter became possible after algebraic symbolism came to maturity in the sixteenth century, allowing calculations with polynomials to be made just as easily as with numbers. By the 1630s, Fermat and Descartes were able to give an algebraic solution of a problem that is usually solved by calculus today: finding the tangents to an algebraic curve.

这个问题的设定如今已为中学生所熟悉。平面上每一点 P 由一个有序数对 (x,y) 给出，其中

The setup for this problem is one that is now familiar to high school students. Each point P in the plane is given by an ordered pair (x,y) of numbers, where

x=从原点 O 到 P 的水平距离 / horizontal distance to P from the origin O,y=从原点 O 到 P 的垂直距离 / vertical distance to P from the origin O.

代数曲线是这样一种曲线：它的点满足方程 p(x,y)=0，其中 p 是多项式。例如，到 O 的距离为 1 的点满足 x2+y2=1，所以单位圆的方程是 x2+y2−1=0。另一个例子是抛物线 y=x2，即 y−x2=0。

An algebraic curve is one whose points satisfy an equation p(x,y)=0, where p is a polynomial. For example, the points at distance 1 from O satisfy x2+y2=1 so the equation for the unit circle is x2+y2−1=0. Another example is the parabola y=x2, or y−x2=0.

这导致了按多项式次数对曲线进行分类。若 p 是 1 次的——即 p(x,y)=ax+by+c——则 p(x,y)=0 是一条直线的方程。若 p(x,y) 是 2 次的，那么费马和笛卡尔（各自独立地）发现，p(x,y)=0 是希腊人研究过的圆锥曲线之一。除去退化情形（即切割圆锥的平面与圆锥交于一点或直线），这些曲线就是椭圆、抛物线和双曲线。这三类曲线的典型例子见图 11。

This leads to a classification of curves by the degree of the polynomial. If p is of degree 1 – that is p(x,y)=ax+by+c – then p(x,y)=0 is the equation of a line. If p(x,y) is of degree 2, then Fermat and Descartes discovered (independently) that p(x,y)=0 is one of the conic sections studied by the Greeks. Apart from degenerate cases, where the plane cutting the cone meets it in a point or lines, these are the ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas. Typical examples of these three types are shown in Figure 11.

曲线 k 的切线，是在某一点与 k “重”相交的直线 l；这里“重”的意思是：把 l 中 y 的表达式代入方程 p(x,y)=0，所得关于 x 的方程有重解。这一精确的代数条件刻画了如下模糊的想法：l 与 k 只交于一个孤立点 P，但任何经过 P 且靠近 l 的直线 l′ 都与 k 交于 P 以及 P 附近至少另一点 P′。图 12 显示了这种情形。当直线 l′ 趋近于 l 时，l 的“二重接触点” P 就是 l′ 的两个接触点 P,P′ 的极限。

Now a tangent to a curve k is a line l that meets k at a point ‘multiply’, in the sense that there is a multiple solution to the equation for x that results from substituting the expression for y in l in the equation p(x,y)=0. This precise algebraic condition captures the vague idea that l meets k at a single isolated point P, but that any line l′ through P and close to l meets k in P and at least one other point P′ near P. Figure 12 shows the situation. The ‘double contact point’ P of l is the limit of the two contact points P,P′ of l′, as the line l′ approaches l.

例如，直线 y=2x−1 在 x=1 处与抛物线 y=x2 相切，因为把 y=2x−1 代入 y=x2，得到方程 2x−1=x2，即 x2−2x+1=0。这个方程可以改写为 (x−1)2=0，这表明它有二重解 x=1。

For example, the line y=2x−1 is tangent to the parabola y=x2 at x=1, because when we substitute y=2x−1 in y=x2 we get the equation 2x−1=x2, or x2−2x+1=0. This equation can be rewritten (x−1)2=0, which shows that it has the double solution x=1.

类似的计算（如果曲线的次数更高，自然会更复杂）使我们能求出任何代数曲线的切线。然而，求代数曲线与 x 轴之间的面积则是一个难得多的问题，即使对曲线 y=1/x 也是如此。正是在这里，对微积分的需求变得迫切起来。

Similar calculations (though naturally more complicated if the curve has higher degree) allow us to find the tangents to any algebraic curve. However, finding the area between an algebraic curve and the x-axis is a more formidable problem, even for the curve y=1/x. This is where the need for calculus becomes acute.

4.3 无穷小微积分

4.3 Infinitesimal Calculus

相切的代数判据陈述起来很简单，尽管用起来可能很困难。一个更严重的异议是，它只适用于代数曲线，而有些在物理上很自然的曲线并不是代数曲线。一个著名的例子是悬链线，即悬挂的链条所呈现的形状。悬链线看起来很像抛物线，但并不是，因此需要另一种方法来求它的切线。

The algebraic criterion for tangency is simple to state, though it can be hard to use. A more serious objection is that it applies only to algebraic curves, and some physically natural curves are not algebraic. One famous example is the catenary, the shape of a hanging chain. The catenary looks rather like a parabola, but it is not, so another method is needed to find its tangents.

事实上，即使对代数曲线，也需要一种更简单的方法——一种能求出任一点处斜率的方法。更好的方法是微分学，这一体系产生于对被称为无穷小的假想实体的代数与几何研究。

In fact, even for algebraic curves a simpler method is desirable – one that finds the slope at any point. A better method is that of differential calculus, a system that arose from the algebra and geometry of hypothetical entities called infinitesimals.

许多早期的微积分倡导者都使用过无穷小，始于 1630 年代，并在 1680 年代莱布尼茨的无穷小微积分中臻于成熟。莱布尼茨为无穷小引入了 dx,dy,dz 之类的记号，他似乎把无穷小看作比普通数更小、但又不为零的量。例如，曲线在点 (x,y) 处的斜率，被看作 (x,y) 与曲线上“无穷接近” (x,y) 的点 (x+dx,y+dy) 之间的斜率 dy/dx。

Infinitesimals were used by many of the early exponents of calculus, starting in the 1630s and coming to maturity with the infinitesimal calculus of Leibniz in the 1680s. Leibniz introduced the notations dx,dy,dz and the like for infinitesimals, which he seemed to view as quantities smaller than ordinary numbers, yet non-zero. For example, the slope of a curve at a point (x,y) was viewed as the slope dy/dx between (x,y) and a point (x+dx,y+dy) on the curve ‘infinitesimally close’ to (x,y).

给定曲线的方程 y=f(x)，一般很容易算出斜率 dy/dx。以抛物线 y=x2 为例。此时

Given an equation y=f(x) for the curve, it was generally easy to calculate the slope dy/dx. Take the parabola y=x2 for example. In this case,

dy=(x+dx)2−x2=2xdx+(dx)2,

所以

so

dydx=2xdx+(dx)2dx=2x+dx.

到了这一步，人们便放心地忽略 dx，并得出结论：对 x 的任何值，y=x2 的斜率都是 2x。（特别地，当 x=1 时斜率为 2，因此该点处切线的方程是 y=2x−1，这与上一节用常规代数求得的结果一致。）

At this stage one feels free to neglect dx and conclude that the slope of y=x2 for any value of x is 2x. (In particular, when x=1 the slope is 2, so the equation of the tangent at this point is y=2x−1, as found by conventional algebra in the previous section.)

用 dx 和 dy 进行的类似计算，可以轻松求出任何代数曲线在曲线上任一点处的斜率，从而求出切线。特别地，y=xn 的斜率是 nxn−1。

Similar calculations with dx and dy easily yield the slope of any algebraic curve, and hence the tangent, at any point on the curve. In particular, the slope of y=xn is nxn−1.

但这只是无穷小魔力的小小一瞥。它们还使曲边面积的计算成为可能，例如曲线 y=f(x) 下方的面积。为此，我们把面积看作 x 的函数 A(x)，取的是固定值 a 与变量值 x 之间的区域，如图 13 所示。x 的无穷小增量 dx 产生面积的无穷小增量 dA，我们可以写作

But this is just a small taste of the magic of infinitesimals. They also allow the calculation of curved areas, such as the area under a curve y=f(x). To do this one views the area as a function A(x) of x, taking the region between a fixed value a and a variable value x, as in Figure 13. An infinitesimal increase dx in x produces an infinitesimal increase dA in area, which we can write

dA=f(x)dx,

因为额外的面积窄条 dA 的宽度为 dx，高度与 f(x) 只相差一个无穷小量。（我们再一次选了一个方便的时机来忽略无穷小。）两边同除以 dx，我们得出

since the extra strip dA of area has width dx and height that differs only infinitesimally from f(x). (We are again choosing a convenient moment to neglect infinitesimals.) We conclude, dividing both sides by dx, that

dA(x)dx=f(x).

换言之，A(x) 是这样一个函数：它的图像的斜率为 f(x)。因此，求曲线下的面积是求斜率的逆问题。如果 f(x) 是我们已经作为斜率 dy/dx 求出过的函数，那么我们可以断定面积函数 A(x) 与 y 相同，至少相差一个常数。

In other words, A(x) is a function whose graph has slope is f(x). Thus finding areas under curves is the inverse problem to finding slopes. If f(x) is a function we have already found as a slope dy/dx, then we can conclude that the area function A(x) is the same as y, at least within a constant.

例如，若 A(x) 是抛物线 y=x2 下方 0 与 x 之间的面积，则

For example, if A(x) is the area under the parabola y=x2 between 0 and x, then

dAdx=x2,

于是我们可以断定 A(x)=13x3，因为当 y=13x3 时 dydx=x2，而且函数 A(x) 与 y 在 x=0 时取值相同。

and we may conclude A(x)=13x3, because dydx=x2 when y=13x3, and the functions A(x) and y agree when x=0.

简言之，这就是莱布尼茨的无穷小微积分。面积问题与切线问题之间的互逆关系被称为它的基本定理。牛顿发现了类似的微积分，只是没有方便而富有启发性的 dx 记号。无穷小微积分的技艺，基本上就是无穷小的代数与几何，再加上对何时“忽略”无穷小的良好判断。（例如，在忽略 dx 之前，先除以 dx！）

This, in a nutshell, is the infinitesimal calculus of Leibniz. The inverse relation between the area and tangent problems is called its fundamental theorem. Newton discovered a similar calculus, though without the convenient and suggestive dx notation. The art of infinitesimal calculus was basically the algebra and geometry of infinitesimals, allied with some good judgement about when to ‘neglect’ infinitesimals. (For example, divide by dx before neglecting it!)

4.4 无穷小：批评与回避

4.4 Infinitesimals: Criticism and Avoidance

无穷小有点像虚数。它们似乎与公认的原理相矛盾——正如虚数与平方为正的原理相矛盾，无穷小与第 2.4 节所述的几何量的阿基米德公理相矛盾——然而它们却使原本困难或不可能的计算成为可能。对十七、十八世纪的数学家来说，这一般就是接受它们的充分理由。

Infinitesimals were a bit like imaginary numbers. They seemed to contradict accepted principles – just as imaginaries contradicted the principle that squares are positive, infinitesimals contradicted the Archimedean axiom for geometric quantities, stated in Section 2.4 – yet they enabled calculations that were otherwise difficult or impossible. For mathematicians of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries this was generally good enough reason to accept them.

但在另一方面，无穷小并不像虚数。虽然虚数确实不属于普通的数系，但很容易扩大这个数系以容纳它们——例如像哈密顿在 1835 年所做的那样，把虚数定义为普通数的有序对。要扩大数系以包含无穷小，就远没有那么容易或方便了。直到二十世纪，人们甚至还不知道这是可能的，而那时数学家们早已决定，最好像欧几里得和阿基米德回避无穷那样回避无穷小。

But in another way infinitesimals were not like imaginaries. While it is true that imaginaries are not part of the ordinary number system, that system can easily be enlarged to accommodate them – for example, by defining imaginaries as ordered pairs of ordinary numbers, as Hamilton did in 1835. It is not nearly as easy, or convenient, to enlarge the number system to include infinitesimals. It was not even known to be possible until the twentieth century, long after mathematicians had decided that it was better to avoid infinitesimals the way Euclid and Archimedes avoided infinity.

在无穷小微积分的初创时期，用穷竭法替换无穷小论证还相当容易，尽管很繁琐。但随着无穷小代数与几何的威力日增，人们对其正确性的信心也越来越强，以古人严格的方式重写论证就成了一件吃力不讨好的事。早在 1659 年，惠更斯就写道：

When infinitesimal calculus was in its infancy it was fairly easy, though tedious, to replace infinitesimal arguments by the method of exhaustion. But as infinitesimal algebra and geometry grew in power, and faith in its correctness grew stronger, it became a thankless task to rewrite arguments in the rigorous ancient manner. As early as 1659, Huygens wrote,

如果几何学中的发现（其数量与日俱增，在这个科学的时代看来很可能发展到巨大的规模）继续按照古人的方式以严格的形式呈现，数学家们将永远没有足够的时间去阅读所有这些发现。（见 Huygens 1659，第 337 页）
Mathematicians will never have enough time to read all the discoveries in Geometry (a quantity which is increasing from day to day and seems likely in this scientific age to develop to enormous proportions) if they continue to be presented in a rigorous form according to the manner of the ancients. (see Huygens 1659, 337)

哲学家们正确地嘲笑了无穷小的概念——贝克莱称之为“逝去量的幽灵”——因为数学家们使用它们的方式松散，有时甚至不一致。但数学家们并没有完全摒弃无穷小，直到出于数学的原因被迫如此。而当他们这样做时，那是一场全面的数学革命的一部分，这场革命在数学基础中用算术取代了几何。我们将在接下来的两节中看到这是如何发生的。

Philosophers rightly mocked the concept of infinitesimals – Berkeley called them ‘ghosts of departed quantities’ – because of the loose and sometimes inconsistent way they were used by mathematicians. But mathematicians did not completely dispense with infinitesimals until forced to do so for mathematical reasons. And when they did it was part of a general revolution in mathematics that replaced geometry by arithmetic in the foundations of mathematics. We will see how this came about in the next two sections.

4.5 复分析

4.5 Complex Analysis

微积分与虚数虽然都出身可疑，却在十八、十九世纪结成了强大的联盟。最引人注目的盟友是圆函数与指数函数，它们在十七世纪被分别研究，并被发现可以用无穷级数来表示。约在 1670 年，牛顿发现了指数函数的级数

Calculus and imaginary numbers, though both had dubious origins, formed a powerful alliance in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The most remarkable allies were the circular and exponential functions, which were studied separately in the seventeenth century and found to be expressible by infinite series. Around 1670 Newton discovered the series for the exponential function,

ex=1+x1!+x22!+x33!+⋯,

他和其他人还重新发现了早已在印度被发现的正弦与余弦级数：

and he and others rediscovered the sine and cosine series that had already been discovered in India:

cos⁡x=1−x22!+x44!−x66!+⋯,sin⁡x=x1!−x33!+x55!−x77!+⋯.

在 ex 的级数中把 x 换成 ix，就得到了奇妙的公式

Replacing x by ix in the series for ex yields the miraculous formula

eix=cos⁡x+isin⁡x,

这是欧拉（1748）发现的。这个公式不仅使正弦和余弦可以用指数来表示，即

discovered by Euler (1748). This formula not only allows sine and cosine to be expressed in terms of exponentials, namely

cos⁡x=12(eix+e−ix),sin⁡x=12i(eix−e−ix),

而且还引起人们注意它们的“双曲”类似物：

but also draws attention to their ‘hyperbolic’ analogues:

cosh⁡x=12(ex+e−x),sinh⁡x=12(ex−e−x).

这种类比或许有助于解释兰伯特（1766，§82）的一个大胆猜想。兰伯特引入了双曲函数，并且无疑了解涉及正弦和余弦的球面三角公式。于是他可能猜想，涉及双曲正弦和双曲余弦的类似公式描述的是“虚半径球面”上的三角学。如果是这样，就可以解释他 1766 年的猜想：非欧几何或许在一个虚球面上成立。（关于非欧几何和兰伯特的虚球面，另见第 6.2 节和第 6.5 节。）

This analogy may help to explain a wild conjecture of Lambert (1766, §82). Lambert introduced the hyperbolic functions and was no doubt aware of the formulas of spherical trigonometry, which involve sine and cosine. He may then have guessed that the analogous formulas involving hyperbolic sine and cosine describe trigonometry on a ‘sphere of imaginary radius’. If so, this could explain his 1766 conjecture that non-Euclidean geometry may hold on an imaginary sphere. (See also Sections 6.2 and 6.5 for more about non-Euclidean geometry and Lambert’s imaginary sphere.)

4.6 哲学问题

4.6 Philosophical Issues

在讨论微积分之前，应当提一下笛卡尔（1637）那本代数几何著作的一个重要副产品——长度的乘法。正如我们在第 1.3 节提到的，长度有一种自然的和，它本身仍是一个长度；但欧几里得及其后继者把两个长度之积看作一个矩形，这严重限制了任何长度的代数。

Before discussing calculus, there is an important by-product of the Descartes (1637) book on algebraic geometry that should be mentioned – multiplication of lengths. As we mentioned in Section 1.3, there is a natural sum of lengths which is itself a length, but Euclid and his successors took the product of two lengths to be a box, which severely curtailed any algebra of lengths.

但还有另一种定义长度之积的方法，它基于相似三角形的比例关系（图 14）。为此，我们选取一个单位长度，即图 14 中标为 1 的长度，并按图示位置构造包含长度 a 和 b 的相似三角形。于是由比例关系可知，正如长度 1 的延续是长度 b，长度 a 的延续就是长度 ab。

But there is another way to define product of lengths, based on the proportionality of similar triangles (Figure 14). To do so we choose a unit length, marked 1 in Figure 14, and construct the similar triangles containing the lengths a and b in the positions shown. Then it follows by proportionality that, just as the continuation of length 1 is length b, the continuation of length a is length ab.

笛卡尔利用这一事实来定义长度之积，从而赋予长度一种与数相似的代数结构。他还指出了求任意长度的平方根的一种简单几何作图（同样涉及相似三角形）。因此，笛卡尔（1637）扫除了由无理长度的存在所引起的一些古老问题：长度毕竟确实像数一样运作，而任何数的平方根也是一个数，这是合理的。

Descartes used this fact to define the product of lengths, thus giving lengths an algebraic structure like that of numbers. He also pointed out a simple geometric construction (also involving similar triangles) for the square root of any length. Thus Descartes (1637) swept away some of the ancient problems posed by the existence of irrational lengths: lengths did behave like numbers after all, and it was reasonable for the square root of any number to be a number.

然而，一个哲学困难刚被消除，微积分又制造了另一个。事实上，微积分的发明对数学哲学的扰动，或许超过了自无理量的发现以来的任何事件。哲学家们正确地质疑了无穷小的概念，但数学家们起初对他们的批评置之不理，仍然相信自己可以用欧几里得的方法得到微积分的结果（尽管他们很少真的这样做）。这一僵局直到 1800 年以后才被打破，那时数学家们不得不承认，欧几里得毕竟不足以作为数学的基础。

But, as soon as one philosophical difficulty was removed, calculus created another. In fact, the invention of calculus disrupted the philosophy of mathematics perhaps more than any event since the discovery of irrational quantities. Philosophers rightly questioned the concept of infinitesimal, but mathematicians at first ignored their criticisms and continued to believe they could obtain calculus results by Euclid’s methods (though they seldom actually did so). There was a stalemate which would not be broken until after 1800, when mathematicians had to concede that Euclid was, after all, not an adequate foundation for mathematics.

直觉与逻辑。直觉在微积分中起着主导作用（至今依然如此）：人们用“曲线上无穷接近的点”和“无穷细的窄条”来建立计算切线和面积的方程。但一旦方程被找到，（无穷小代数中）代数符号的力量便占了上风。数学家们相信微积分，是因为它在解决几何和力学问题上取得了惊人的成功。他们还认为自己立足于坚实的基础之上，相信所有结果都能用穷竭法严格地得到。

Intuition and logic. Intuition played a leading role in calculus (and still does), where ‘infinitesimally close points on a curve’ and ‘infinitesimally thin strips’ were used to set up equations for calculating tangents and areas. But, once the equations were found, the force of algebraic symbolism (in the algebra of infinitesimals) prevailed. Mathematicians believed in calculus because of its amazing success in solving problems in geometry and mechanics. They also thought they were on solid ground, believing that all their results could be obtained rigorously by the method of exhaustion.

意义与存在。然而，正如贝克莱所指出的，无穷小的存在是非常可疑的，那么，是什么解释了它们的成功呢？（在贝克莱之前，霍布斯曾严厉批评微积分以及在几何中使用代数。但他提出了一种站不住脚的关于圆的说法——声称圆只包含有限多个点——并声称借此解决了古老的“化圆为方”问题，从而在数学家面前丧失了信誉。）

Meaning and existence. Yet, as Berkeley pointed out, the existence of infinitesimals was highly dubious, so what explained their success? (Before Berkeley, Hobbes had made harsh criticisms of calculus and of the use of algebra in geometry. But he destroyed his credibility with mathematicians by proposing an untenable account of the circle – claiming that it contains only finitely many points – and claiming thereby to solve the ancient problem of ‘squaring the circle’.)

离散与连续。另一方面，无穷小在离散与连续之间提供了一座新的桥梁（尽管摇摇欲坠）。连续统的图景并不清晰，或许还自相矛盾，但人们却能正确地计算长度和面积。那么，无穷小或许有助于解释连续统的本性？

Discrete and continuous. Then again, infinitesimals provided a new bridge (albeit rickety) between the discrete and continuous. The picture of the continuum was unclear, and perhaps contradictory, yet one could correctly calculate lengths and areas. So perhaps infinitesimals could help explain the nature of the continuum?

从长远来看，人们发现由无穷小引起的问题是关于连续统本性的问题，特别是关于它作为一种特殊无穷集合的本性的问题。在接下来的两节中，我们将看到这个问题及其哲学含义是如何展开的。

In the long run, the problems raised by infinitesimals were found to be problems about the nature of the continuum, and particularly its nature as a particular kind of infinite set. In the next two sections we will see how this problem, and its philosophical implications, unfolded.

5 连续函数与实数

5 Continuous Functions and Real Numbers

预览

PREVIEW

微积分能够处理许多具体函数，但一般的函数概念仍然模糊。约在 1800 年，有必要证明连续函数的一些一般性质——令人惊讶的是，这是为了证明代数基本定理。在十八世纪对这一定理作过一些可疑的证明尝试之后，高斯提出了几个证明。其中最令人信服的是高斯（1816）中的证明，它把定理化归为奇数次多项式的特殊情形。这样的多项式 p(x) 的取值会“连续地”从正值（当 x 为很大的正数时）变到负值（当 x 为很大的负数时）。于是看起来显然，这个多项式会在某处取值 0，正如基本定理所要求的那样。

Calculus could deal with many specific functions, but the general function concept remained vague. Around 1800, it became necessary to prove some general properties of continuous functions – surprisingly, in order to prove the fundamental theorem of algebra. After some dubious attempts to prove this theorem in the eighteenth century, Gauss proposed several proofs. The most convincing was one in Gauss (1816), which reduced the theorem to the special case of odd-degree polynomials. Such a polynomial p(x) takes values that change ‘continuously’ from positive (for large positive x) to negative (for large negative x). It then seems obvious that the polynomial takes the value 0 somewhere, as required for the fundamental theorem.

波尔查诺（1817）指出了高斯证明中的关键假设，即连续函数的介值定理：如果当 x 变化时 f(x) 是一个从负值连续变化到正值的函数，那么对某个 x 值有 f(x)=0。波尔查诺能够给出连续性的令人满意的定义，但为了证明介值定理，他不得不假定实数的一条性质，即最小上界性质：如果 S 是一个有界的实数集，那么 S 有最小上界。

Bolzano (1817) put his finger on the key assumption of Gauss’s proof, the intermediate value theorem for continuous functions: if f(x) is function that varies continuously from negative to positive as x varies, then f(x)=0 for some value of x. Bolzano was able to give a satisfactory definition of continuity, but to prove the intermediate value theorem he had to assume a property of the real numbers, the least upper bound property: if S is a bounded set of real numbers, then S has a least upper bound.

从欧几里得的几何实数概念出发，不可能证明最小上界性质，而在此之前人们一直认为这一概念是充分的。人们终于不得不着手处理调和离散与连续这一未竟之事。

It was not possible to prove the least upper bound property from Euclid’s geometric concept of real number, which had been thought adequate until then. It was finally necessary to grapple with the unfinished business of reconciling the discrete with the continuous.

5.1 代数基本定理

5.1 The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
